items.back: The three main styles of Indian temple architecture (north, south, and hybrid Deccan).

items.front: Distinguish Nagara vs Dravida temple towers and gateways.
items.back: Nagara: curvilinear shikhara, no boundary gopuram. Dravida: pyramidal vimana over the sanctum, gateway gopuram, enclosure & tank.

items.front: Building 'kalyana mandapas' was a notable feature of temples in which kingdom?
Evolutionary phases of the Dravida style?
items.back: Pallava (Mahabalipuram rathas, Shore Temple) → Chola (Brihadeeswara, Rajaraja I) → Vijayanagara (Hampi, Lepakshi) → Nayaka (Madurai gopurams).

items.front: The Vesara style is associated with which dynasties?
items.back: The Chalukyas of Badami/Kalyani and the Hoysalas (star-shaped soapstone temples).

items.front: The three early schools of Indian sculpture and their materials?
items.back: Gandhara (grey schist, Greco-Buddhist), Mathura (red sandstone, indigenous), Amaravati (white/greenish limestone).

items.front: Who built the rock-cut Kailasa temple at Ellora?
items.back: The Rashtrakutas (Krishna I) — a monolithic Dravida-style temple.

items.front: Why is Ellora distinctive among cave complexes (UPSC 2018)?
items.back: It has Hindu, Buddhist AND Jain monuments together (incl. the Kailasa temple).

items.front: Lepakshi (Anantapur) Veerabhadra temple — style and famous feature?
items.back: Vijayanagara style; a celebrated hanging pillar, fresco ceilings and a giant monolithic Nandi.

items.front: Amaravati school of sculpture — material and patrons?
items.back: White/greenish limestone with narrative Buddhist reliefs and 'empty throne' aniconism; patronised by the Satavahanas & Ikshvakus.

items.front: Undavalli caves (Guntur) are known for what?
items.back: A rock-cut monolithic reclining Vishnu (Anantasayana), of the Vishnukundina era.

items.front: Ramappa (Rudreshwara) temple — dynasty, engineering, UNESCO year?
items.back: Kakatiya (Palampet); 'floating' sandbox foundation & light bricks; UNESCO World Heritage 2021; named after sculptor Ramappa.
Qutb Shahi; Indo-Saracenic/Indo-Islamic, granite & lime, four minarets.
Trabeate = beam-and-lintel (Hindu temple tradition); arcuate = arches, domes and vaults (Islamic) with lime mortar.
